title: pvWritePPLYWriter
body:
## pvWritePPLYWriter

Explicit-export writer for Stanford PLY (.ply): polygonal surface geometry (points and polygons) for mesh, 3-D printing and point-cloud tools, binary by default (FileType). It accepts polygonal data only, so extract a surface first (pvExtractSurface). Field arrays are not carried, except optional per-point or per-cell RGB(A) colours written when EnableColoring is true, ColorArrayName names the array and a lookup-table resource is attached to the export. Publication uses the geometry contract: Schemaxis re-reads the file with ParaView's PLY reader and compares the triangulated surface within the tolerance.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Colours need all three: EnableColoring true, ColorArrayName and a LookupTable resource in the export's resources; otherwise the writer writes geometry only.
- With ChooseArraysToWrite true, keep the colour array in the lists or no colours are written; the geometry comparison accepts the dropped fields, so array selection stays available here.
- An earlier catalogue run (verification/2026-09-16-catalogue-expansion.json, writerQualification) passed only on a small serial fixture with a tolerance of 1e-6 and the other options at their defaults; no current native acceptance check is recorded, so verify the export on representative data.

Native constructor: `PPLYWriter`. Identity: `writers/PPLYWriter`. Role: `writer`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Connect upstream object to `Input` | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPolyData"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |
| `LookupTable` | Connect upstream object to `LookupTable` | False | one object | `lookup-table` | `{"compatibility":"native-proxy-group","cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","rating":"unknown"},"nativeGroup":"lookup_tables"}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellDataArrays` | Select the cell data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `ChooseArraysToWrite` | Explicitly choose which arrays to write. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `ColorArrayName` | The array that will be used for saving color information when **Enable Coloring** is ON. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE","REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `EdgeDataArrays` | Select the edge data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `EnableAlpha` | Specify whether alpha channel information should be saved in the PLY file. If enabled, the data source's transfer function from the active view will be used. This property is disabled if EnableColoring isn't enabled. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `EnableColoring` | When true, the writer maps the array named in ColorArrayName through the lookup table attached as the export's LookupTable resource and stores the resulting RGB colours per point or per cell in the PLY file. Without both the array and the lookup table it writes geometry only. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `FieldDataArrays` | Select the field data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileType` | The type for the data file (i.e. ascii or binary). | `{"type":"enum","values":["Ascii","Binary"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Ascii"` |
| `NumberOfIORanks` | In parallel runs, this writer can consolidate output from multiple ranks to a subset of ranks. This specifies the number of ranks that will do the final writing to disk. If **NumberOfIORanks** is 0, then all ranks will save the local data. If set to 1 (default), the root node alone will write to disk. All data from all ranks will be gathered to the root node before being written out. | `{"minimum":0,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0` |
| `PointDataArrays` | Select the point data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `RankAssignmentMode` | When **NumberOfIORanks** is greater than 1 and less than the number of MPI ranks, this controls how the ranks that write to disk are determined. This also affects which ranks send data to which rank for IO. In **Contiguous** mode (default), all MPI ranks are numerically grouped into **NumberOfIORanks** groups with the first rank in each group acting as the `root` node for that group and is the one that does IO. For example, if there are 16 MPI ranks and NumberOfIORanks is set to 3 then the groups are `[0 - 5], [6 - 10], [11 - 15]` with the first rank in each group 0, 6, and 15 doing the IO. In **RoundRobin** mode, the grouping is done in round robin fashion, thus for 16 MPI ranks with NumberOfIORanks set to 3, the groups are `[0, 3, ..., 15], [1, 4, ..., 13], [2, 5, ..., 14]` with 0, 1 and 2 doing the IO. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Contiguous","RoundRobin"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Contiguous"` |
| `RowDataArrays` | Select the row data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `VertexDataArrays` | Select the vertex data arrays to pass through. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Output publication contract:

```json
{
  "comparison": "geometry",
  "extensions": [
    "ply"
  ],
  "filenames": "managed output directory",
  "losses": [
    "fields",
    "point-identity",
    "interior-cells",
    "structure"
  ],
  "qualification": "requires fixture",
  "time": "one scheduled state"
}
```

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "explicit exports with semantic readback",
  "outputPorts": 0,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `scenes[].exports`; writers cannot be graph nodes. The main data input is `node`; non-data ports go in `resources`.

```json
{
  "id": "exportResult",
  "node": "DATA_NODE",
  "writer": "pvWritePPLYWriter",
  "acceptLosses": [
    "fields",
    "point-identity",
    "interior-cells",
    "structure"
  ]
}
```
